newsitem.title: INDIA: Iran, India foreign ministers hold Afghan talks.
newsitem.headline: Iran, India foreign ministers hold Afghan talks.

text.p: Indian and Iranian foreign ministers began hastily arranged talks on Thursday on regional issues, including the stepped-up civil war in Afghanistan.
Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told reporters he would discuss "everything" with Indian External Affairs Minister Inder Gujral but declined to give details.
Velayati was due to meet Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda later on Thursday before returning to Teheran.
Velayati had been scheduled to arrive in New Delhi on Wednesday but his trip was delayed, Indian officials said.

The Iranian minister was on a lightning tour of the former Soviet republics of Central Asia to discuss Afghanistan, where government forces are battling Islamic Taleban militia who drove them out of the capital late last month.
He told reporters in Almaty on Wednesday that the crisis in Afghanistan could not be resolved by force and called on all factions to negotiate a peaceful settlement.
"We believe that (the) Afghanistan problem doesn't have a military solution," Velayati said after discussing the fighting in Afghanistan with Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev.
"All factions should sit down together, talk together to reach a peaceful settlement in Afghanistan," he told reporters.
Neighbouring Pakistan on Tuesday offered to mediate between the warring factions.

But that offer was unlikely to suit officials in Iran or India, where media have accused Pakistan, the United States and Saudi Arabia of provoking a crisis inside the country torn by years of civil war.
Both Iran and India recognise the ousted government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, driven out of the Afghan capital last month.
Velayati's talks with Indian officials would precede a visit by Indian Vice President Kocheril Raman Narayanan to Iran starting on October 22.

The Foreign Ministry said at the weekend it was following fighting in Afghanistan with deep concern and that the fall of Kabul to Taleban militia had created "a dangerous new situation of great fluidity".
Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral was quoted on Tuesday as saying New Delhi continued to recognise the ousted government of Rabbani.
India supported efforts by U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali and his special representative to bring peace to Afghanistan, the Foreign Ministry statement said.
